`0.html` was a bare `<!DOCTYPE html><title>0</title>`, so I added the three things a minimal page is usually missing and left it otherwise as it was:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>0</title>
```

- **`lang="en"`** tells screen readers and translation tools the language; I assumed English.
- **`charset="utf-8"`** makes the encoding explicit, so non-ASCII characters don't get garbled.
- **`viewport`** makes the page render at device width on mobile instead of a zoomed-out desktop layout.

I kept the `<head>` and `<body>` tags omitted as in the original; this is still valid HTML. I did not run it through a validator or open it in a browser.

## What changed

- **Dark mode support:** added `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">` so the page follows the system theme instead of always rendering white.
- **Readable base styles:** added a small `<style>` block with a 40rem centred column, padding, the system font and 1.5 line height.
- **Content landmark:** added `<main>` with an `<h1>`, so the page is no longer blank and has a heading for screen readers.

## What changed
- **Text size on iOS:** added `text-size-adjust: 100%` so Safari doesn't inflate the text when the phone is rotated to landscape.
- **Heading line height:** the `h1` was inheriting the body's 1.5, which is loose for large text and shows once a heading wraps; it's now 1.2.
- **Heading wrapping:** `text-wrap: balance` evens out the lines of a multi-line heading.
- **Heading margin:** removed the top margin so the heading doesn't stack on the body padding, and set the bottom margin to `1rem`.

## What I left alone
- **Structure:** the omitted `<head>` and `<body>` tags are valid HTML and look deliberate, so I kept that style.
- **Content:** the title and heading are both still "0". I didn't invent a real title or a `<meta name="description">`; those are the most useful next additions once you know what the page is for.
